However, there is currently no pre-operative or intraoperative diagnostic test that is capable of accurately identifying all cancer cells, especially at the leading tumor edge where there is only microscopic disease. Thus, to ensure no cancer cells are left behind, a border of grossly normal appearing tissue (up to 2 cm) is also removed during surgery. Yet, in the oral cavity, removal of bordering healthy tissue is typically associated with severe structural, functional and cosmetic side effects. Most notably, the ability to eat may be compromised. There is an urgent need for intraoperative diagnostic tests that can delineate healthy from cancer tissue in real-time. The aim of this study is to evaluate the use of florescence lifetime imaging with Protophoryin IX (a natural intermediate in the iron pathway that fluoresces under blue light) to accurately diagnose cancer versus normal tissue during surgery. We will also characterize the tissue changes that drive differences in florescence emission
